In this statement, a "crash" is a situation in which the database is shut down abruptly (e.g. due to a power outage, a server failure, or a bug in the software).
A write-ahead log (WAL) is a record of all modifications made to a database. When a modification is made to a database, a record of that modification is first written to the log before it is written to the database itself. This record in the log includes the modification, such as an insert or update, and a pointer to the location in the database where the modification was made. The log is stored in a safe location, such as a separate disk drive or a redundant array of independent disks (RAID), so that it is not affected by a crash. When the database is shut down abruptly, the log contains a record of all modifications that were made to the database just before the crash.
To recover from a crash, the database system reads the log and reapplies all the modifications recorded in it. This is done by playing back the log, in order, and applying each modification to the database. When the playback is complete, the database is restored to a consistent state, as if it had not crashed. The log also provides a way to roll back
